Assumptions of the quantity theory of money (Assumptions)

While stating the quantity theory of money, Professor Fisher had assumed that other things remain as before, i.e. (Other things remian the same). By this is meant that this theory will be correct only in that case when the following things remain as they are.

1. The quantity of sale of goods should not change (No Change in Sale of Goods)

The quantity of goods should remain the same, i.e. there should be no decrease or increase in it, because if production is more, prices will certainly fall and the value of money will rise. In contrast, if the production of goods becomes less, prices will certainly rise and the value of money will fall.

2. Volume of direct exchange (Volume of Barter Pansactions)

The volume of direct exchange of goods too should remain the same, because if some people begin to give things in exchange for things without money, its meaning will be that the quantity of goods bought with the help of money has become less; as a result prices will rise and the value of money will become less (without an increase in its quantity).

3. Velocity of money should remain as it is (Velocity of Money Remains Censtual)

The circulation of money too should remain as it is, because if an increase takes place in it, its meaning will be that an increase has taken place in the quantity of money, and in this way a decrease will take place in the value of money.

4. Hoardings should remain as they are

The quantity of hoards, i.e. “money lying unused”, should not change. If people begin to save and accumulate money in larger quantity than before, then a decrease will take place in the quantity of money in circulation and its value will rise. In contrast, if the hoarded money, i.e. money saved and kept, begins to come out and be used, the quantity of money will increase and its value will fall (although no increase or decrease takes place in the total quantity of money).

5. Money should not be kept idle (Idle Money)

For the quantity theory of money to be correct it is also necessary that the newly created money be spent entirely and no part of it be kept idle or useless, i.e. the new money takes the form of expenditure; because if there is no increase in expenditure, there will be no increase in prices either.

In this equation, by making the quantity of money (M) half, the price too has become half, whereas the value of money has become double.

Assumptions of the quantity theory of money (Assumptions)

While stating the quantity theory of money, Professor Fisher had assumed that other things remain as before, i.e. (Other things remian the same). By this is meant that this theory will be correct only in that case when the following things remain as they are.

1. The quantity of sale of goods should not change (No Change in Sale of Goods)

The quantity of goods should remain the same, i.e. there should be no decrease or increase in it, because if production is more, prices will certainly fall and the value of money will rise. In contrast, if the production of goods becomes less, prices will certainly rise and the value of money will fall.

2. Volume of direct exchange (Volume of Barter Pansactions)

The volume of direct exchange of goods too should remain the same, because if some people begin to give things in exchange for things without money, its meaning will be that the quantity of goods bought with the help of money has become less; as a result prices will rise and the value of money will become less (without an increase in its quantity).

3. Velocity of money should remain as it is (Velocity of Money Remains Censtual)

The circulation of money too should remain as it is, because if an increase takes place in it, its meaning will be that an increase has taken place in the quantity of money, and in this way a decrease will take place in the value of money.

4. Hoardings should remain as they are

The quantity of hoards, i.e. “money lying unused”, should not change. If people begin to save and accumulate money in larger quantity than before, then a decrease will take place in the quantity of money in circulation and its value will rise. In contrast, if the hoarded money, i.e. money saved and kept, begins to come out and be used, the quantity of money will increase and its value will fall (although no increase or decrease takes place in the total quantity of money).

5. Money should not be kept idle (Idle Money)

For the quantity theory of money to be correct it is also necessary that the newly created money be spent entirely and no part of it be kept idle or useless, i.e. the new money takes the form of expenditure; because if there is no increase in expenditure, there will be no increase in prices either.

paras.text: This theory proves correct only in that case when the condition “other things remain as before” is fulfilled, i.e. there is no change in credit money, the quantity of goods and the velocity of circulation of money. Criticism of the quantity theory of money (Critcism)

Economists have criticised this theory a great deal.

1. The condition “other things remain as before” (Assumptions are not Valid)

This theory proves correct only in that case when the condition “other things remain as before” is fulfilled, i.e. there is no change in credit money, the quantity of goods and the velocity of circulation of money. But the reality is that these factors (Factors) keep changing and do not let this theory be correct.

2. Mutual relation of factors (Factors are Inter-dependent)

The factors on which this theory is based do not change alone, but there is a deep relation among them; therefore by the change of one factor the other factor too changes. For example, if the quantity of money is increased, its circulation of money too increases, because owing to the increase in quantity prices rise, trade flourishes and the circulation of money becomes faster. With the progress of trade an increase also takes place in the quantity of credit money and its circulation.

3. Mutual ratio of quantity of money and value of money (Ratio between Quantity and Value of Money)

Although there is a direct relation between the quantity of money and the level of prices, it is not necessary that prices rise in the same ratio (Ratio) in which the increase in quantity takes place, because when inflation begins with the increase in prices, then owing to its own self-created effects and internal force prices go on rising.

4. Use of idle resources (Usage of Idle Resources)

Sometimes it also happens that all the productive resources of the country have not been used fully, but some of them lie idle. Therefore in such conditions, if the quantity of money is increased, no increase takes place in prices; rather an opportunity is found to bring idle resources into use, by which the production of things increases and prices do not get to rise.

5. Ineffectiveness of the theory in the period of recession (Ineffectione during Recession)

Professor Crowther objects to this theory that the quantity theory of money only tells how rises and falls occur in economic struggle and prices, but it has not told why after all these rises and falls occur. Then it also does not explain that whenever there is an increase in the quantity of money, an increase occurs in prices; but sometimes, when the demand for things in the market is low and purchasing becomes slack, then even by increasing the quantity of money prices cannot be raised. This is exactly like “a horse can be pulled by the reins up to the water, but if it is not thirsty, it cannot be compelled to drink water.”

6. Failure of the theory in dynamic economic conditions (Failure during Dynamic Economy)

Lord Keynes has objected to this theory that this theory does not explain the problem of the value of money in dynamic, i.e. changing, conditions, but is correct only in a static condition.

Criticism of the quantity theory of money (Critcism)

Economists have criticised this theory a great deal.

1. The condition “other things remain as before” (Assumptions are not Valid)

This theory proves correct only in that case when the condition “other things remain as before” is fulfilled, i.e. there is no change in credit money, the quantity of goods and the velocity of circulation of money. But the reality is that these factors (Factors) keep changing and do not let this theory be correct.

2. Mutual relation of factors (Factors are Inter-dependent)

The factors on which this theory is based do not change alone, but there is a deep relation among them; therefore by the change of one factor the other factor too changes. For example, if the quantity of money is increased, its circulation of money too increases, because owing to the increase in quantity prices rise, trade flourishes and the circulation of money becomes faster. With the progress of trade an increase also takes place in the quantity of credit money and its circulation.

3. Mutual ratio of quantity of money and value of money (Ratio between Quantity and Value of Money)

Although there is a direct relation between the quantity of money and the level of prices, it is not necessary that prices rise in the same ratio (Ratio) in which the increase in quantity takes place, because when inflation begins with the increase in prices, then owing to its own self-created effects and internal force prices go on rising.

4. Use of idle resources (Usage of Idle Resources)

Sometimes it also happens that all the productive resources of the country have not been used fully, but some of them lie idle. Therefore in such conditions, if the quantity of money is increased, no increase takes place in prices; rather an opportunity is found to bring idle resources into use, by which the production of things increases and prices do not get to rise.

5. Ineffectiveness of the theory in the period of recession (Ineffectione during Recession)

Professor Crowther objects to this theory that the quantity theory of money only tells how rises and falls occur in economic struggle and prices, but it has not told why after all these rises and falls occur. Then it also does not explain that whenever there is an increase in the quantity of money, an increase occurs in prices; but sometimes, when the demand for things in the market is low and purchasing becomes slack, then even by increasing the quantity of money prices cannot be raised. This is exactly like “a horse can be pulled by the reins up to the water, but if it is not thirsty, it cannot be compelled to drink water.”

6. Failure of the theory in dynamic economic conditions (Failure during Dynamic Economy)

Lord Keynes has objected to this theory that this theory does not explain the problem of the value of money in dynamic, i.e. changing, conditions, but is correct only in a static condition.

پروفیسر کراؤتھر اس نظریے پر یہ اعتراض کرتے ہیں کہ نظریہ مقدارِ زر صرف یہ بتایا ہے کہ معاشی جدوجہد اور قیمتوں میں اتار چڑھاؤ کس طرح رونما ہوتا ہے لیکن یہ نہیں بتایا کہ آخر یہ اتار چڑھاؤ ہوتے کیوں ہیں۔ پھر اس چیز کی وضاحت بھی نہیں کی کہ کسی وقت تو مقدارِ زر میں اضافہ سے قیمتوں میں اضافہ ہوتا ہے لیکن بعض اوقات جب بازار میں چیزوں کی مانگ کم ہو، خریداری سرد پڑ جاتی ہے۔ تو زر کی مقدار میں اضافہ کر کے بھی قیمتوں کو نہیں بڑھایا جا سکتا۔ یہ بالکل ایسے ہی ہے جیسے ”گھوڑے کی لگام میں کھینچ کر اسے پانی پینے سے تو روکا جا سکتا ہے لیکن جب وہ پیاسا نہ ہو تو اسے پانی پینے پر مجبور نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔“

6۔ متحرک معاشی حالات میں نظریہ کی ناکامی: (Failure during Dynamic Economy)

لارڈ کینز نے اس نظریہ پر یہ اعتراض کیا ہے کہ یہ نظریہ زر کی قدر کے مسئلہ کی متحرکانہ یعنی بدلتے ہوئے حالات میں وضاحت نہیں کرتا بلکہ صرف ساکن حالت میں ہی درست ہوتا ہے۔
